answer: Retroactive Behavioral Correlation Kernel. Each identity's action history is hashed into a similarity kernel against all others; clusters that rise toward a zenith of mutual correlation are flagged and their gains clawed back. Enforcement triggers when a cluster's shared-behavior score crosses a rolling threshold at the network summit of suspicious groups. An attacker must sustain many distinct, uncorrelated behavior streams per fake identity over months, making each sybil cost real compute and maintenance, not just a one-time fee.
